sourceEvidence.fact: The published ARM64 Linux asset is built with Rust target aarch64-unknown-linux-musl; no Android target is present in the release matrix.
Herdr depends on libc, interprocess, and a repository-patched portable-pty implementation; Windows-only dependencies are separately gated.
Linux, macOS, and Windows have explicit platform modules. Other target operating systems select the fallback module; target_os=android is therefore not the Linux module.
The fallback is explicitly marked unsupported and stubs daemon detachment, process discovery, process signalling/existence, clipboard, URL opening, notifications, and related platform behavior.
The Unix PTY backend delegates PTY creation and child spawning to the vendored portable-pty implementation.
Unix IPC uses interprocess local sockets with filesystem socket paths and Unix metadata/permission operations.
The Linux build relies on Linux /proc process metadata plus Unix process-group and signal APIs for foreground-job and agent/process behavior.

upstreamSupportSignal.note: Absence of issues is not support proof; it only records that no explicit upstream Termux/Android issue signal was found during this review.

nativeAndroidSourceBuild.reason: A native Android Rust target would compile target_os=android and select Herdr's unsupported fallback platform module, so it cannot be treated as feature-complete migration evidence.

linuxMuslPrebuiltOnTermux.reason: The exact official Linux-musl ARM64 asset may be tested as an ephemeral executable on the Android kernel only after exact size and SHA-256 verification. This does not authorize installation or server startup.
allowedActions: download the exact release asset into a temporary private directory
verify exact byte size and SHA-256 before making it executable
execute only --version with isolated temporary HOME/XDG state and a bounded timeout
write sanitized local untracked execution evidence
remove the temporary binary and sandbox on exit
forbiddenActions: copy or symlink the binary into PREFIX/bin or another persistent executable path
create or attach a Herdr workspace/session
run Herdr update or installer commands
mutate Android device_config, phantom-process limits, or battery policy
linuxMuslPrebuiltOnTermux.successGate: verified digest plus exit code 0 from the exact asset's --version command with output identifying Herdr 0.8.0
linuxMuslPrebuiltOnTermux.failureGate: any download, size, digest, exec, timeout, signal, or identity failure keeps tmux canonical and records the failure without installation

proofCeiling: Pinned source inspection proves the release build target and source platform routing. It approves only an ephemeral checksum-verified --version execution probe of the exact Linux-musl ARM64 release asset. It does not prove Android support, authorize installation or server startup, prove PTY/IPC/process detection, persistence, detach/reattach, agent state, background survival, sprint success, or tmux retirement.
